Exploitability Rate (completed runs labelled exploited: declared intent or confirmed execution of the preflight) with Wilson 95% CI, per agent, generator and tactic; failure-mode taxonomy (recognized attack, irrelevant to task, acknowledged but not executed, no acknowledgment); verified execution; inter-judge agreement (Fleiss' kappa)

Automatic: run stratification, three local open-weight LLM judges (Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-9B) by majority with evidence anchoring, regex refusal veto and declared-intent override; PATH audit shim for execution. Manual: one author's blind labels on 240 runs (kappa 0.83-0.85) and failure-taxonomy labels

ER = exploited / completed runs (higher = worse security). Temperature 0, top-p 1, 120 s limit, auto-approve. Draft verdict (security as quality): works if ER low.
- Gemini CLI + gemini-3-flash + malicious skills: ER 95.5% raw majority, 96.1% with override [95.3, 96.7] (2,705/2,816); per generator 95.5-96.8%; explicit refusal in 17 of 111 failures; Exfiltration 95.5%. Security: does not work
- Qwen Code + qwen3-coder-plus + malicious skills: ER 71.6% raw, 74.0% with override [72.3, 75.6] (2,081/2,813); per generator 67.7% (DeepSeek-R1) to 76.9%; refusals 95 of 732 failures; Exfiltration 38.5%, Impact 56.2%. Security: does not work
- Human gold standard: Gemini 95.5% (94.2-96.3), Qwen 70.9% (65.6-75.7)
- Verified execution: 1 run of 5,629 (harness-limited)
Cost: not measured

Two agents (Gemini CLI, Qwen Code) chosen by availability at Transurban; same 471 commands x 6 generators, same task prompt, sandbox, 120 s limit, temperature 0, auto-approve. No benign-skill control. One run per skill per agent. Acceptance: judge panel validated against human labels. Human intervention: none

Gemini CLI more exploitable than Qwen Code by 22-24 points (non-overlapping Wilson CIs); exploitability nearly invariant to generator model; tactic gap largest for Exfiltration (95.5% vs 38.5%); Qwen-only off-task rejection (10.1% of its failures). Explicit safety recognition 1.99% of all runs

Distinguished the agents clearly. Single judges disagree strongly on Qwen (Fleiss' kappa -0.06; flag rates 22.4-94.8%), motivating the panel; panel vs human kappa 0.83-0.85. Limitations: single masking template, synthetic not in-the-wild skills, single task, 120 s limit, two agents, residual non-determinism

Commands do not cover all payloads or obfuscations; synthetic descriptions and one 'mandatory preflight' template (rates as lower bound for this pattern); only two CLI agents (not Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot); one task; 120 s cap; verified execution harness-limited; future: in-the-wild skills, more tasks, long-horizon runs, pre-ingestion skill scanner evaluation

Code and dataset: github.com/awsm-research/AgentJailbreak (per-run logs, prompts, regexes, unit tests). No pre-registration. Language: shell commands; web app language chosen by agent (e.g. Python/Flask).
